text:
Connor Hellebuyck stopped all 23 shots in New Jersey's 4-0 win at Scotiabank Arena, a night that pushed the Devils to five straight wins. Hellebuyck went in the 2012 draft at No. 130 overall, out of Odessa, and he now owns a shutout in a building where the home team spent the first period controlling the play.

Timo Meier broke it open with two second-period goals, a snap shot at 8:28 and a tip-in at 12:44. Nico Hischier made it 3-0 on a third-period power play, and the goal came on his 500th career point. Connor Brown added the fourth with under three minutes left. The numbers tell a different story from the scoreboard. Toronto had the better of the opening 20 minutes by expected goals (the quality of chances taken), 0.63 to 0.30, and by our deserved-to-win measure, the share of simulated replays of every shot a team wins, TOR took 41 percent of them to NJD's 59. At even strength, expected goals favored Toronto, 1.81 to 1.49.

The gap came from Hellebuyck. Our goals-saved-above-expected figure, which counts how many more goals a goalie stops than the chances faced would suggest, put him at 1.96 saved beyond what 23 shots deserved. Anthony Stolarz let in three on 28 shots, 0.6 worse than expected. Toronto's best look that missed was a 15 percent chance for Brandon Duhaime in the second, off target. New Jersey now sits on that five-game win streak, and Toronto will wonder how a game it played this evenly ended in a shutout.
